citation: V. N. Rodionov, A. M. Mandel, "Violation of the Equivalence Principle in Non-Hermitian Fermion Theory", Russ. Phys. J. 61, 1376 (2018), doi:10.1007/s11182-018-1545-9 (journal; not on arXiv)
summary: Same school as the previous entry. A gamma5 extension of the Dirac mass term breaks the weak equivalence principle; the condition m2/m1 = m1/2M <= 1 preserves it for Standard Model fermions to high accuracy, and the same condition yields a new class of solutions whose properties make them dark-matter candidates. A companion conference paper (Rodionov, Kravtsova, Mandel 2019, doi:10.1142/9789811202339_0072, INSPIRE recid:1738434) states an inertial-gravitational 'paradox' for the exotic particles.
difference: Dark matter is a new solution class of a modified Dirac equation tied to a maximal mass, not conjugate (momentum-polarized) ordinary matter. The inertial-gravitational mass split ascribed to the exotic particles weighs against identifying C1's chi with them, since chi falls exactly like ordinary matter.

quotes.text: a new class of solutions of the modified Dirac equation arises that describes particles whose properties make them obvious candidates for dark matter
such procedure inevitably leads to violation of the weak equivalence principle, i.e., causes an inequality of gravitational and inert fermion masses

citation: V. N. Rodionov, A. M. Mandel, G. A. Kravtsova, "Restriction of the Fermion Mass Spectrum in PT-Symmetric Systems and its Implications for Studying Dark Matter", Theor. Math. Phys. 198, 412 (2019), doi:10.1134/S0040577919030061 (journal; not on arXiv). The same claim first appeared in Rodionov and Mandel, arXiv:1708.08394 (2017; arXiv preprint only).
summary: Kadyshevsky lineage (de Sitter momentum space of radius M, the 'fundamental mass'). Rodionov's school recasts Kadyshevsky's geometric model as a non-Hermitian Dirac theory with a gamma5 mass term and a maximal mass M, and conjectures that the 'exotic' fermions present in both versions are constituents of dark matter. It continues the known Kadyshevsky, Mateev, Rodionov and Sorin 2007 (0708.4205, C1 related), where the exotic fermion field comes from a second factorization of the de Sitter momentum-space wave operator and its quanta are conjectured to be dark matter. The titles of the 26 and 24 INSPIRE citers of 0708.4205 and hep-ph/0512332, and an abstract filter on the citers of the older Kadyshevsky papers, show no other dark-matter proposal.
difference: The exotic fermions are a new fermion species whose polarization and mass properties are fixed by the curvature of momentum space; they are not ordinary matter in the mirror polarization, are not organized or localized in momentum, and carry no velocity gate or momentum clumping. The same authors state that such particles violate the weak equivalence principle (Russ. Phys. J. 2018, separate entry), the opposite of C1's chi, which gravitates exactly like ordinary matter.

quotes.text: Exotic particles appear in both these theories. A detailed consideration of the properties of these particles allows conjecturing that they are possible candidates in the structure of dark matter.
A consistent approach to this problem requires the constraint m ≤ M, where M bounds the entire fermion mass spectrum.

citation: X. Chu, C. Garcia-Cely, H. Murayama, "Velocity Dependence from Resonant Self-Interacting Dark Matter", Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 071103 (2019), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.122.071103; arXiv:1810.04709 (journal)
summary: This bears on the χ form's observable, not on its mechanism. A resonance in dark-matter self-scattering gives a cross section large at dwarf-galaxy velocities and small at cluster velocities, the pattern row 1 of #11 §13 attributes to the gate. The analysis is model-independent and needs no light mediator. It is a published ordinary-physics route to the dwarf-strong, cluster-weak knee besides the Yukawa power law that row 1 lists as the standard expectation.
difference: The velocity dependence comes from a Breit-Wigner resonance in the relative momentum of ordinary position-local particles. It is not a gate from momentum-space wavepacket overlap, and there is no conjugate matter. Whether a resonance's tail can be told from the gate's tail (row 3's discriminant) is not assessed here.

difference: The momentum-space monopole is a background gauge field (a Berry-curvature source in a crystal or in the kinematics of spinning particles), not a population of magnetically charged objects; no dark matter, no abundance, no account of the null result.

summary: Pseudo-complex general relativity (pc-GR) starts from Born's point that quantum mechanics treats coordinates and momenta on an equal footing. It extends the coordinates to X = x + I y, with y_μ = A l u_μ, a minimal length times the four-velocity (the Born–Caianiello velocity-space part). In the pc-Robertson–Walker model (§4.5) the scale factor becomes a = a_R + I a_I, and to leading order a_I = l ȧ_R(0)/a_R⁴: the velocity-like partner shrinks as our scale factor grows ('it continues to be even smaller for larger times'). The paper ties the growth of a_I toward the Big Bang to 'a dominance of the dark energy' there. It obtains today's acceleration from a dark-energy density Λ a_R^{3(β−1)}, which for β = 1 is a cosmological constant.

Its law is a_I ∝ a_R⁻⁴, not a·ã = 1, and there is no conjugate matter, no collapse and no w_eff = −w̃. The pseudo-imaginary part is velocity space in Caianiello's sense, not a spontaneously selected polarization.

summary: A theory built on Born reciprocity: the action is S + S̃, the second term written on a separate energy-momentum manifold with its own FRW-type 'dual universe' (scale factor ã(e) in the energy e), linked to spacetime by a generalized Fourier transform; x↔p duality sets the fundamental cosmological constant to zero.
